Container.Name: 24seven-Traefik
Container.Overview: A lightweight, modern, self-hosted calendar. Make events (one-off and recurring), get email or browser (Web Push) reminders, colour-code your events, import/export iCalendar (.ics), and sync to your phone with any CalDAV client. It does what you want — and just that. This variant ships with Traefik labels preconfigured for calendarit.home.lab.
Container.Description:
24seven (CalendarIT) — a lightweight, self-hosted calendar (React web UI + ASP.NET Core REST API), preconfigured to sit behind Traefik. The container carries Traefik labels that route Host(`calendarit.home.lab`) to nginx on container port 80 — no published host port required as long as Traefik reaches this container over a shared Docker network (set Network to the same custom network your Traefik container uses, e.g. proxynet, and point calendarit.home.lab at your Traefik IP in your local DNS). Recurring events (RRULE) with correct time zones and DST, colour-coded categories, email and browser (Web Push) reminders and invitations, and iCalendar (.ics) import/export. This single-container build runs the React UI behind nginx and the API together in one image, storing data in a built-in SQLite database (or point it at your own Postgres). Mount /data to your appdata share so your events and uploaded avatars survive container updates. A JWT signing key is auto-generated and persisted under /data on first run; set your own JWT Signing Key to override.
Invitations and reminders are sent through each user's own mail account, connected inside the app under Settings — Email. The optional Server Mail settings give the server an account of its own for activation links and password resets.
Create your own account first: the first account is active at once and is the admin. Everyone who signs up after it must be activated — by an emailed link (set the Server Mail settings and Public Base URL) or by you in Settings → Users. Set Disable Registration to true once everyone has an account.

Config.Name: App Data
Config.Description: Host folder where 24seven stores its SQLite database, uploaded avatars, and the auto-generated JWT signing key. Point this at your appdata share to persist data across updates.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id the app runs as (it starts as root only to take ownership of the App Data folder, then drops to this user). 99 is Unraid's 'nobody'.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id the app runs as. 100 is Unraid's 'users'.

Config.Name: Mail Host Policy
Config.Description: Optional. Which addresses users' mail servers (Settings → Email) may point at: private (internet and your LAN, never this server itself), public (internet only), or any (also loopback, e.g. a mail bridge running in this container's network). Empty = public while anyone can sign up (so a stranger's account can't reach into your network), private once Disable Registration is true.

Config.Name: Server Mail Host
Config.Description: Optional. The server's own outgoing mail server, used only for account mail: activation links for new sign-ups (needs Public Base URL) and password resets. New accounts can't sign in until activated; without this, the admin (the first account) activates them in Settings → Users, or you run: docker exec -u 99 <container> dotnet /app/calendarITCore.dll activate-account user@example.com

Config.Name: Server Mail Port
Config.Description: Optional. 587 (STARTTLS, default) or 465 (TLS on connect).

Config.Name: Server Mail Username
Config.Description: Optional. Login for the server mail host; empty for a relay that needs none.

Config.Name: Server Mail Password
Config.Description: Optional. Password for the server mail host.

Config.Name: Server Mail From
Config.Description: Optional (required with Server Mail Host). The sender, e.g. 24seven <noreply@example.com>.

Config.Name: Server Mail TLS on Connect
Config.Description: Optional. true = TLS from the first byte (port 465), false = STARTTLS. Empty = true for port 465, else false. TLS is required either way.

Config.Name: API Rate Limit
Config.Description: Optional. Requests per account (per IP before sign-in) per minute across the API and CalDAV, with bursts up to the same number for a phone's first sync. 0 turns it off.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Networks
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated networks your reverse proxy connects from (e.g. 172.16.0.0/12). Only those are believed about a visitor's IP address. Leave empty while nothing but your proxy can reach this container.

Config.Name: Traefik Enable
Config.Description: Tells Traefik's Docker provider to pick this container up. Leave at true — set to false only to take the container out of Traefik without removing it.

Config.Name: Traefik Router Rule
Config.Description: Traefik routing rule for the web UI. Default routes the hostname calendarit.home.lab to this container — make sure your local DNS (e.g. Pi-hole/AdGuard/Unbound) resolves it to your Traefik instance. Change the hostname here if you use a different domain.

Config.Name: Traefik Entrypoint
Config.Description: Which Traefik entrypoint serves this router — must match an entrypoint name from your Traefik static config (commonly web for HTTP :80, websecure for HTTPS :443, or http/https depending on your setup).

Config.Name: Traefik Service Port
Config.Description: Container port Traefik forwards traffic to. CalendarIT's nginx listens on 80 inside the container — leave this at 80.

Config.Name: JWT Signing Key
Config.Description: Optional. Secret (at least 32 characters) used to sign login tokens. LEAVE EMPTY to auto-generate one and persist it under /data (recommended). Set your own only if you need a fixed key across multiple instances; changing it later signs everyone out.

Config.Name: Environment
Config.Description: Optional. Production (default) or Development. Development also exposes the OpenAPI document at /openapi/v1.json.

Config.Name: Database Provider
Config.Description: Optional. Sqlite (built-in, default — recommended for most self-hosters) or Postgres. If set to Postgres, also fill in the Postgres Connection string.

Config.Name: Postgres Connection
Config.Description: Optional. Full Npgsql connection string, required only when Database Provider is Postgres. Example: Host=192.168.1.10;Port=5432;Database=calendarit;Username=calendarit;Password=secret. Ignored while Database Provider is Sqlite.

Config.Name: Disable Registration
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true once everyone who needs an account has one. Your server is reachable by anyone who knows its address — that is what makes phone sync work — so while sign-up is open strangers can create accounts. They can't sign in until activated (by the emailed link, or by the admin in Settings → Users), and the admin gets a notice. Existing accounts keep working and the Register tab disappears from the sign-in screen.

Config.Name: Public Base URL
Config.Description: Optional — needed for links in emails (password reset, account activation, the admin's new-account notice): the address users actually type, e.g. https://calendar.example.com. Links are built from this and never from the request, because the address in a request is a header anyone can set — otherwise a stranger could have a working reset link mailed to a site of their choosing. Leave empty and those emails aren't sent; sign-in and everything else still work.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Hops
Config.Description: Optional. How many proxies sit in front of the app, used to work out each visitor's real IP address (which the login rate limit and the logs rely on). 2 is right for this template: Traefik, then the nginx inside the container. Add one for every further proxy in the chain — counting too few makes every visitor look like one address, too many lets visitors fake theirs.

Config.Name: Auth Rate Limit
Config.Description: Optional. How many sign-in, registration, and token-refresh requests one IP address may make per minute before being turned away. The default suits a household; raise it only if legitimate users share one address and hit the limit.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Optional. Minimum log level written to the container log: Verbose, Debug, Information (default), Warning, Error, or Fatal.

Config.Name: VAPID Public Key
Config.Description: Optional. Public half of the VAPID key pair that signs browser (Web Push) reminder notifications. LEAVE EMPTY to auto-generate a pair on first run and persist it under /data (recommended) — browser notifications then work with no setup. Set your own (both keys) only to keep the same keys across multiple instances or rebuilds.

Config.Name: VAPID Private Key
Config.Description: Optional. Private half of the VAPID key pair (keep secret). Leave empty to auto-generate it alongside the public key. Only set this if you also set the VAPID Public Key.

Config.Name: VAPID Subject
Config.Description: Optional. Contact URI sent to push services with each notification, e.g. mailto:admin@example.com. Leave empty to use the built-in default. Only relevant when browser notifications are used.
